chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan narrated from Ali ibn Asbat from Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the qals (eye kohl), does it break the fast of the fasting person? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.الْقَلْسِ: Eye kohl or cosmetic powder applied to the eyes

ai.seo_question: Does applying eye kohl break the fast in Islam?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that applying *qals* (kohl) does not break the fast, addressing a specific point of fiqh regarding external applications. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes between substances that reach the stomach and those that remain external, reinforcing the principle that fasting is invalidated only by deliberate ingestion. The narration highlights the practical ease granted to believers in maintaining worship without unnecessary hardship.
